text:
You need about 300 to 400 W of solar panels to fully recharge a 1000 Wh power station in one sunny day. I worked this out from the rule of thumb in the guides you found, and I didn't open any of the pages.

**Formula** (the same one Enough Watts gives [3]): daily energy (Wh) = panel watts × peak sun hours × 0.75. The 0.75 covers real-world losses from heat, angle, wiring and charge conversion.

Rearranged, panel watts needed = 1000 ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day recharge |
|---|---|
| 5 (sunny summer) | about 270 W |
| 4 (typical) | about 335 W |
| 3 (winter or cloudy) | about 445 W |

**Smaller panels** still work, but they take longer. A 200 W panel makes about 600 Wh a day at 4 peak sun hours, so a full recharge takes about 1.7 days. A 100 W panel takes 3 days or more.

**Check your station's solar input limit.** Many 1000 Wh units accept only 200 to 500 W of solar input. A bigger array than that won't charge it any faster.
